A dev-server 500 on /explore appeared mid-check and was diagnosed rather than assumed: build:frontend passed throughout and a clean dev restart compiled /explore in 205ms and served 200, so it was a stale Next module cache, not a regression.

non_blocking_findings: D-0024 and D-0031 remain open, so every leaf was judged by its testcase name and executed count rather than an exit code.

The exploration error copy is proven by its unit leaf and by direct source inspection, not by a live failure: with the backend stopped, the session guard intercepts first and renders its own message, so the exploration-specific copy is not reachable that way without changing code.
A missing migration surfaces as an unhandled 500 rather than anything diagnosable - observed live before the dev app DB was migrated. Already covered by D-0033 and D-0039; no new deferral raised.

functional.summary: LIVE end-to-end check against real Bedrock, run from THIS worktree's own servers after confirming their cwd - the servers found running on 3000/4000 belonged to the ask-surfaces worktree and were replaced, since a check against them would have exercised task 2's build, which has no Explore page at all. Bedrock verified configured in this tree by behaviour, not by reading secrets: provider bedrock, region ap-south-1, model id set, bearer token present. The whole loop works: ask a real question, save it, pin it, reopen both, delete. The model-bypass re-run is proven two independent ways rather than asserted - the original Bedrock ask took 1434ms while the re-run of the same stored selection took 38ms, and the audit row for the re-run carries model_id NULL. The audit question is the DERIVED label 'Actual · Budget', not a fabricated sentence. Pinned cards render metadata only and caused NO fan-out: exactly 2 /api/chat calls existed in total (the original ask and the one re-run) and loading the dashboard added none.
manual_validation_steps: Confirmed the servers on 3000/4000 were THIS worktree by process cwd before trusting anything (they were not - the ask-surfaces worktree's were running and were replaced).

GET /api/pins returned 500 on first load. Diagnosed rather than assumed: the dev app DB held only the 9 auth/audit tables, so task 3's 0001_saved_and_pins.sql had never been applied here. Ran db:migrate, which added exactly saved_queries and dashboard_pins - environment state, not a code defect.
Explore / Saved renders href=/explore in the shell nav - a live destination, where it had no href before this task.
/explore matches the prototype: eyebrow EXPLORE, heading 'Saved views', the line 'Selections you can reopen without rebuilding the filter row.'
Asked a real governed question via a suggested chip. Answer returned with the VERIFIED badge: actual, budget - Governed financial, ACTUAL 0.00, BUDGET 9877956.93.

Save view and Pin report controls are present on the successful answer and both created (POST /api/saved 201, POST /api/pins 201) - the controls that did not exist before this task and without which task 3's routes were unreachable.
The saved row is labelled 'Actual · Budget' from the shared catalog constant, with 'Month: 2026-09-01-2026-09-12' as its filter summary - real labels, not raw ids.
Opened the saved view: it navigated to /ask and rendered through task 2's existing renderer, with the turn labelled 'Actual · Budget' and the same figures from a fresh execution.
Model bypass proven: original ask POST /api/chat 1434ms (Bedrock) vs re-run 38ms; audit rows show event_type request with question 'Actual · Budget' and model_id NULL for the re-run.
Dashboard Pinned reports renders title and month with Open/Delete and NO figure. Total /api/chat calls stayed at 2 across the whole session, so the dashboard performed no fan-out.
Deleted the pin from the dashboard: DELETE /api/pins/:id 200 and the empty state returned ('Pin a successful Ask answer to keep it on this dashboard.').
Exploration audit trail confirmed in the database: exploration.pins.request x8 and exploration.saved.request x3, so task 3's fail-closed audit fires on these surfaces.

A dev-server 500 on /explore appeared after the design passes; build:frontend passed throughout and a clean dev restart compiled /explore in 205ms and served 200, confirming a stale Next module cache rather than a regression.
non_blocking_findings: The exploration error copy was verified by unit leaf and source inspection rather than live: stopping the backend makes the session guard intercept first with its own message, so the exploration-specific copy is not reachable that way without changing code.

The mandatory design skills took three delegate runs and still were not both applied by the worker: frontend-design showed zero occurrences in all three job logs while the third run's summary CLAIMED it was applied. The orchestrator read frontend-design/SKILL.md directly and applied it, which found a real defect - the surfaces rendered 'API request failed with status 500' to the user because use-exploration.ts passed ApiError.message through verbatim. Fixed in use-exploration.ts with per-surface load and delete copy naming what the reader can do next; ApiError itself was left alone because it is shared by every surface.

emil-design-eng was genuinely read and applied on the second pass (440 lines read); the quality floor it covers is met on evidence - prefers-reduced-motion present, 20 focus-visible rules, 3 responsive breakpoints, role=alert on error regions.
